_comment: The one place this documentation deployment's constants live. Every script here reads this
file, so a name or a path changes in ONE place. It carries NO secrets and is tracked.
This stack is PURELY STATIC. It is documentation for a public npm package: no chain access,
no database, no secrets, no volume, nothing to back up. It reads nothing from the keykeeper
deployment on the same host and writes nothing anywhere. A wipe costs a rebuild, not data.
⚠ It is NOT part of the fuji fleet. keykeeper-network/deploy/fuji/topology.json drives the
keepers, verifiers, accountants and the explorer, and its render.sh regenerates that
compose file with a 'do not edit' banner. This stack lives beside them the same way the
Tasra Vault relayer and the health demo do: its own project, its own ingress script.

_ip_comment: web-server. The A record points here and Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 is answered here, so the
⚠ sdk.t3-foundry.fuji.tasra.network is THREE labels below the apex, so Cloudflare's
Universal SSL does not cover it even if someone did orange-cloud it — the certificate
has to come from Let's Encrypt at the origin either way.

host._comment: Its own tree. Nothing else on the host reads or writes it.

_dns_comment: The public name is https://sdk.t3-foundry.fuji.tasra.network — operator's choice of label.
⚠ It must match `site` in ../../site/astro.config.mjs. Astro bakes that value into the
canonical <link>, the sitemap and the OpenGraph URLs, so a mismatch is invisible in the
browser and wrong in every crawler and social preview.
